name: Timing Exterior Repaints Between Tenants in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How should landlords in Los Angeles County time exterior repainting between tenants to minimize vacancy but still allow proper curing and inspections?
mainEntity.text: How should landlords in Los Angeles County time exterior repainting between tenants to minimize vacancy but still allow proper curing and inspections?

acceptedAnswer.text: For Los Angeles County landlords, exterior repainting is both a maintenance task and a marketing opportunity, but improper timing can extend vacancies or annoy new tenants. Ideally, work is planned to begin in the final weeks of an outgoing tenant’s lease, with clear communication about parking, noise, and protected entryways. Once surfaces are prepped and painted, most modern exterior paints are dry to touch quickly but continue curing for days. Leaving at least several clear-weather days after final coats are applied helps reduce the risk of damage from moving, cleaning, or last-minute repairs. Schedule your final inspection and any professional photography after this cure window so the home presents at its best. If repainting must occur between tenants, try to group all exterior work, including minor stucco or wood repairs, into a single mobilization. Discuss with your contractor whether any areas will remain tacky or more vulnerable during showings, and plan pathways accordingly. Clarify in the contract that punch-list items will be addressed before the new tenant’s move-in date. Careful planning allows you to upgrade curb appeal without extending downtime or compromising paint performance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Landlords should schedule exterior repainting to start near the end of a lease, allowing a few clear-weather days after completion for curing and inspections before new tenants move in. Coordinating access, parking, and noise windows reduces disruption while ensuring the paint job is not rushed.
